name: hcapp_setFcmTokens
description: Updates the Apple Push Notification (APNS) and Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) tokens for the calling device, called after the OS grants or refreshes notification permissions (@apnsToken is NULL on Android). Auth: HC6.ValidateAppAuth (spNumber 15); no permission gate — a device may only set its own tokens. A fresh FCM token stamps FcmTokenCreatedAt and clears FcmTokenDeleted. Since 2026-09-17 it also retires the same physical device's other rows so one hasher stops receiving duplicate pushes: (a) any other HC.Device row carrying the identical FCM token string (any hasher — one token = one install), and (b) on iOS/iPadOS only, the same hasher's other Apple rows with the same DeviceData identifierForVendor. Android is deliberately excluded from (b) because its fingerprint is identical across two handsets of one model.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Registered device UUID. Used as the auth lookup key and the UPDATE target.

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived cryptographic token validated by HC6.ValidateAppAuth against the device secret.

parameters.name: apnsToken
parameters.description: Apple Push Notification Service token. NULL for Android devices. Matches Device.ApnsToken NVARCHAR(500) NULL.

parameters.name: fcmToken
parameters.description: Firebase Cloud Messaging token. NULL if not yet available. Matches Device.FcmToken NVARCHAR(500) NULL.

rowsets.name: Envelope
rowsets.description: Always returned first. success=1 (errorCode/errorType NULL) on success; success=0 with errorCode and errorType on any error: ValidateAppAuth codes (1160/1360/1260 family) or 1915 / errorType 19 from the CATCH block.

columns.name: success
columns.description: 1 if the operation succeeded; 0 on any error path.

columns.name: errorCode
columns.description: NULL on success. Populated error code on failure (auth or DB error).

columns.name: errorType
columns.description: NULL on success. HC6 error type code on failure: 11=auth, 19=db.

rowsets.name: ErrorDetail
rowsets.description: Returned as the second rowset only when success=0. Contains structured error detail for the caller.

columns.name: errorId
columns.description: GUID of the HC.ErrorLog entry created for this error.

columns.name: errorCode
columns.description: Error code forwarded from ValidateAppAuth, or 1915 from the CATCH block.

columns.name: errorTitle
columns.description: Short error title. 'Unexpected error' from the CATCH block path.

sideEffects: UPDATE HC.Device SET ApnsToken, FcmToken, FcmTokenCreatedAt = SYSUTCDATETIME() and FcmTokenDeleted = NULL (both only when @fcmToken is not NULL) WHERE id = @deviceId. FcmTokenCreatedAt / FcmTokenDeleted are DATETIMEOFFSET(7) NULL, added by db/hc6/app/archive/HC6.Device.FcmTokenTimestamps.migration.sql (missing from the stale db/schema/tables/HC.Device.Table.sql).
When @fcmToken is not NULL: UPDATE HC.Device SET FcmToken = NULL, FcmTokenDeleted = SYSUTCDATETIME() on every OTHER row with the same FcmToken string (not scoped to the hasher).
When the calling device is iOS/iPadOS and has an identifierForVendor: the same NULLing on the same hasher's other iOS/iPadOS rows that carry a token and the same identifierForVendor.
INSERT HC.ErrorLog on auth failure (via ValidateAppAuth) and in the CATCH block (after ROLLBACK).

codeSmells.detail: @deviceId, @accessToken (lines 3-4) have no SQL default. A client that omits one is refused by SQL before the procedure runs: no HC.ErrorLog row, an empty 500 in the app, and any graceful check inside is unreachable (CLAUDE.md, Rack of Lamb 2026-09-29).

The UPDATE at line 79 does not verify a row was hit. An unknown @deviceId cannot pass ValidateAppAuth, so this is near-unreachable, but a device row deleted between auth and update would still report success=1.

codeSmells.issue: JSON_VALUE over CAST(DeviceData) in a WHERE clause
codeSmells.detail: Line ~118 evaluates JSON_VALUE(CAST(d.DeviceData AS NVARCHAR(MAX)), '$.identifierForVendor') per row; it is bounded by UserId and FcmToken IS NOT NULL so the row count is small, but it cannot use an index.

breakingChanges: Success rowset shape changed: HC5 returned a single 'result' column (NVARCHAR 'Success'/'Failed'); HC6 returns a structured envelope with success (BIT), errorCode (INT), errorType (INT). All callers must be updated.

Error rowsets restructured: HC5 returned HC5-style standard error columns (errorId, errorType, errorTitle, errorUserMessage, debugMessage, errorProc); HC6 returns the two-rowset pattern (envelope + ErrorDetail). The 'debugMessage' column is no longer present in HC6 error detail.
TRY/CATCH added: HC5 had no error handling; unhandled SQL errors now return success=0 with errorCode/errorType rather than propagating an unhandled exception to the caller.
Auth delegated to HC6.ValidateAppAuth: HC5 used CHECK_ACCESS_TOKEN_V2 directly; HC6 delegates to the shared ValidateAppAuth helper, which may have different token validation semantics.
